answer: A stake-weighted reputation bond resists Sybil attacks in an agent economy: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, like nectar stored for the hive. A single operator spinning up thousands of fake identities faces a cost that grows linearly, while honest agents build a mesa of trust, a broad flat plateau of verified history that cheap clones cannot copy. Bad behavior slashes the bond and sends a ripple through the agent linked reputation graph, so one exposed fraud poisons every sockpuppet tied to the same stake and makes mass fakery unprofitable.
